sections.position: O&G and Energy Transition Marketing Director @ AVEVA
sections.bio:
Most marketing falls flat in industrial B2B because it tries to turn engineers into copywriters or hires marketers who don’t speak engineer.

I do both.

With 20+ years in industrial marketing at companies like AVEVA and Schneider Electric, and as the founder of Blackbird Digital Marketing, I turn technical complexity into customer-centric messaging that actually sells.

I help companies:

- Clarify their value prop
- Translate specs into buyer benefits
- Shorten long sales cycles
- Optimize LinkedIn and websites to convert engineers into leads

Why? Because your product isn’t the problem.
Your message is.

If your website reads like a spec sheet—or your LinkedIn posts get applause but no leads—let’s fix that.

Want messaging that sounds like your best salesperson, not your instruction manual?

Let’s talk.

posts.text:
Most manifestos list what a company believes. This one lists what it will refuse.

No bad-fit retainers. No toxic clients. No work that doesn't move the business.

That's not a values page. That's a qualification filter — the wrong prospect disqualifies themselves before the first call.

Then there's the line most firms would never publish: "Unknown destination yet."

Saying you don't have a roadmap shrinks the top of your funnel on purpose. It filters for people buying how you operate, not where you claim to be headed.

Worth reading if you've ever written a values page nobody used.

Are you curious about what happened in the oil and gas track in Milan at a VIVA World Conference? This is your chance to check out the presentations. 
https://lnkd.in/gcftwtRr

Most search case studies show you a spike. This one shows a floor.

A month of work that individually looks like nothing — internal links, directory listings, Reddit threads, a few listicle placements. None of it would survive a “what did this one thing do for us?” audit.

Then around the 8th the graph stepped up and stayed there.

That’s what compounding looks like from the inside. Unglamorous, unattributable, and then suddenly obvious.

Arobis AI Ran Yosef

Consulting firms entering Saudi Arabia are quietly redesigning the model itself.
Smaller permanent teams. AI absorbing the research and production layer. Specialist expertise assembled per engagement instead of carried on payroll.

Worth sitting with what that actually changes. The pyramid priced junior hours. This model prices judgment and access — different economics, different sales motion, different reason a client picks you.

And the network becomes the real asset. One you have to build long before you need it.

Good breakdown from Abdulrahman Alsheail

Most deep tech launches ask you to book a demo. This one asks you to run one command.
I can’t validate the performance claims and I’m not going to pretend otherwise — nobody can from a feed. But the go-to-market decision is worth studying regardless: when your claim sounds impossible, the only marketing that works is letting people test it before they believe it.

The risk is the mirror image. If the first test disappoints, the install becomes the disproof — publicly, and fast.

Watching this one.

Oh, and will be trying it in Claude and Gemini - I’ll let you know what happens. Thanks Brayon Pieske
